answer: Admission is a trace-cluster bond. An applicant posts a three-epoch time-locked deposit and a runtime transcript bound to a single custody key. New transcripts are clustered against stored hashes; near-duplicates collapse to one seat and surplus deposits are slashed to the reporter. I keep those hashes in a walnut tin so collisions are cheap to detect. This is not a fable about honest farms — the slash is automatic after a challenge window. Each accepted seat writes a sable ink receipt that maps one deposit to one spend path, and withdrawal stays frozen until two quiet epochs pass.
